kept.text: The number of people living with diabetes rose from 200 million in 1990 to 830 million in 2022.
kept.subject: Key facts

kept.text: Prevalence has been rising more rapidly in low- and middle-income countries than in high-income countries.
kept.subject: Key facts

kept.text: More than half of people living with diabetes did not take medication for their diabetes in 2022.
kept.subject: treatment

kept.text: Diabetes treatment coverage was lowest in low- and middle-income countries.
kept.subject: treatment

kept.text: Diabetes causes blindness, kidney failure, heart attacks, stroke and lower limb amputation.
kept.subject: Key facts

kept.text: In 2021, diabetes and kidney disease due to diabetes caused over 2 million deaths.
kept.subject: Key facts

kept.text: In addition, around 11% of cardiovascular deaths were caused by high blood glucose.
kept.subject: Hyperglycaemia

kept.text: A healthy diet, regular physical activity, maintaining a normal body weight and avoiding tobacco use are ways to prevent or delay the onset of type 2 diabetes.
kept.subject: Prevention

kept.text: Diabetes can be treated and its consequences avoided or delayed with diet, physical activity, medication and regular screening and treatment for complications.
kept.subject: treatment

kept.text: Diabetes is a chronic disease that occurs either when the pancreas does not produce enough insulin or when the body cannot effectively use the insulin it produces.
kept.subject: Diabetes

kept.text: Hyperglycaemia, also called raised blood glucose or raised blood sugar, is a common effect of uncontrolled diabetes and over time leads to serious damage to many of the body's systems, especially the nerves and blood vessels.
kept.subject: Hyperglycaemia

kept.text: In 2022, 14% of adults aged 18 years and older were living with diabetes, an increase from 7% in 1990.
kept.subject: Overview

kept.text: More than half (59%) of adults aged 30 years and over living with diabetes were not taking medication for their diabetes in 2022.
kept.subject: treatment

kept.text: In 2021, diabetes was the direct cause of 1.6 million deaths and 47% of all deaths due to diabetes occurred before the age of 70 years.
kept.subject: Overview

kept.text: Another 530 000 kidney disease deaths were caused by diabetes, and high blood glucose causes around 11% of cardiovascular deaths (1).
kept.subject: Overview

kept.text: Since 2000, mortality rates from diabetes have been increasing.
kept.subject: Overview

kept.text: Symptoms of diabetes may occur suddenly.
kept.subject: Symptoms

kept.text: losing weight unintentionally
kept.subject: Symptoms

kept.text: Over time, diabetes can damage blood vessels in the heart, eyes, kidneys and nerves.
kept.subject: Diabetes

kept.text: People with diabetes have a higher risk of health problems including heart attack, stroke and kidney failure.
kept.subject: Diabetes

kept.text: Diabetes can cause permanent vision loss by damaging blood vessels in the eyes.
kept.subject: Diabetes

kept.text: Many people with diabetes develop problems with their feet from nerve damage and poor blood flow.
kept.subject: Symptoms

kept.text: This can cause foot ulcers and may lead to amputation.
kept.subject: Symptoms

kept.text: Type 1 diabetes (previously known as insulin-dependent, juvenile or childhood-onset) is characterized by deficient insulin production and requires daily administration of insulin.
kept.subject: treatment

kept.text: Type 2 diabetes affects how your body uses sugar (glucose) for energy.
kept.subject: Type 2 diabetes

kept.text: It stops the body from using insulin properly, which can lead to high levels of blood sugar if not treated.
kept.subject: Hyperglycaemia

kept.text: Over time, type 2 diabetes can cause serious damage to the body, especially nerves and blood vessels.
kept.subject: Type 2 diabetes

kept.text: Type 2 diabetes is often preventable.
kept.subject: Prevention

kept.text: Early diagnosis is important to prevent the worst effects of type 2 diabetes.
kept.subject: diagnosis

kept.text: The best way to detect diabetes early is to get regular check-ups and blood tests with a healthcare provider.
kept.subject: diagnosis

kept.text: Symptoms of type 2 diabetes can be mild.
kept.subject: Symptoms

kept.text: They may take several years to be noticed.
kept.subject: Symptoms

kept.text: As a result, the disease may be diagnosed several years after onset, after complications have already arisen.
kept.subject: diagnosis

kept.text: More than 95% of people with diabetes have type 2 diabetes.
kept.subject: Type 2 diabetes

kept.text: Gestational diabetes is hyperglycaemia with blood glucose values above normal but below those diagnostic of diabetes.
kept.subject: Gestational diabetes

kept.text: Gestational diabetes occurs during pregnancy.
kept.subject: Gestational diabetes

kept.text: Women with gestational diabetes are at an increased risk of complications during pregnancy and at delivery.
kept.subject: Gestational diabetes

kept.text: These women and possibly their children are also at increased risk of type 2 diabetes in the future.
kept.subject: Gestational diabetes

kept.text: Gestational diabetes is diagnosed through prenatal screening, rather than through reported symptoms.
kept.subject: diagnosis

kept.text: Impaired glucose tolerance (IGT) and impaired fasting glycaemia (IFG) are intermediate conditions in the transition between normality and diabetes.
kept.subject: Impaired glucose tolerance

kept.text: People with IGT or IFG are at high risk of progressing to type 2 diabetes, although this is not inevitable.
kept.subject: Impaired glucose tolerance

kept.text: Lifestyle changes are the best way to prevent or delay the onset of type 2 diabetes.
kept.subject: Prevention

kept.text: To help prevent type 2 diabetes and its complications, people should:
kept.subject: Prevention

kept.text: reach and keep a health body weight
kept.subject: Prevention

kept.text: stay physically active with at least 150 minutes of moderate exercise each week
kept.subject: Prevention

kept.text: eat a healthy diet and avoid sugar and saturated fat
kept.subject: Prevention

kept.text: not smoke tobacco.
kept.subject: Prevention

kept.text: Early diagnosis can be accomplished through relatively inexpensive testing of blood glucose.
kept.subject: diagnosis

kept.text: People with type 1 diabetes need insulin injections for survival.
kept.subject: treatment

kept.text: One of the most important ways to treat diabetes is to keep a healthy lifestyle.
kept.subject: treatment

kept.text: WHO aims to stimulate and support the adoption of effective measures for the surveillance, prevention and control of diabetes and its complications, particularly in low- and middle-income countries.
kept.subject: WHO response

kept.text: In April 2021 WHO launched the Global Diabetes Compact, a global initiative aiming for sustained improvements in diabetes prevention and care, with a particular focus on supporting low- and middle-income countries.
kept.subject: Global Diabetes Compact

kept.text: In May 2022 the World Health Assembly endorsed five global diabetes coverage targets to be achieved by 2030.
